problem: At an ice cream shop, on average, $25%$ of customers buy chocolate ice cream. What is the probability that the $4$th customer of the day is the first person buying a chocolate ice cream? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.

feedback.problem: A fair six-sided die is repeatedly rolled until the number six appears. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability that it will be rolled exactly $2$ times is{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of rolls until a $6$ came on. The probability of getting a $6$ on any roll of the die is

$$
p=\frac{1}{6}.
$$

So, the number of rolls until a $6$ came up can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success $p=\frac{1}{6}.$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(\frac{1}{6}).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={(1-\frac{1}{6})}^{x-1}(\frac{1}{6}) \\  & ={(\frac{5}{6})}^{x-1}(\frac{1}{6})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability of getting a $6$ on the $2$nd roll is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=2) & =f(2) \\  & ={(\frac{5}{6})}^{2-1}(\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =(\frac{5}{6})(\frac{1}{6}) \\  & ≈0.139,\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $3$ decimal places.
